Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The Sri Lankan players make their way out to the middle, followed by Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow. Dushmantha Chameera will start with the ball.

Right then! England need 242 runs to win and with the batting line-up they have, this should not be too difficult a task but Sri Lankan bowlers have done a good job in the previous games and they won't make it easy. What will happen? Do join us in a while for the run chase.

Sam Curran is up for a chat! He says that Oval is a lovely place to play cricket in and also says that he was riding his luck. Adds that the ball swung which was a huge help. States that it is a very good pitch and it will come onto the bat nicely in the second innings.

Sri Lanka made a good recovery as they were 21 for 4 at one stage but to reach 241 is an achievement. Dhananjaya de Silva was the star of the show with the bat as he played some lovely shots in his 91. He deserved a 100 but fell short. Dasun Shanaka played a very handy knock. There were some handy contributions down the order but the main worry for Sri Lanka will be the top order.

England's bowling was led by the two left-armers, Sam Curran and David Willey. The former took 5 wickets while Willey finished with 4. They were brilliant especially Curran who impressed on his home ground. Tom Curran did a good job but was unlucky not to get a wicket while Adil Rashid too did a decent job. They could have got this done early but Sri Lanka made a good recovery.

A good recovery from Sri Lanka after being at 21 for 4 at one stage. They did not look like they will reach even 200 but they have managed to reach 241. It is not a match-winning score as the pitch is very good to bat on and England have a very strong batting line-up but it is a good recovery. England, on the other hand, had another good day with the ball but they will rue the fact that they gave away few runs towards the end.

Good fielding! Length ball on middle, de Silva flicks it through the mid-wicket region. Tom Curran gives it a chase and pulls it back in. Three taken.
Fullish ball outside off, Nissanka looks to cut but it goes off the bottom half of the bat and it goes to third man for a single.
WIDE! Good length ball down the leg side, Nissanka looks to flick but misses.
Fuller length on off, Nissanka defends it back to the bowler.
Good length ball outside off, Nissanka punches it to the off side.
Full and on off, Pathum plays it to cover off the front foot.
Full on off, Nissanka defends it to cover off the front foot.
Fullish ball outside off, de Silva pushes it to cover.
EDGY! Full on off, de Silva looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the new batsman in.
Another review taken by Sri Lanka for LBW. Ultra Edge says there is no spike as the ball passes the bat. The Ball Tracker shows all three reds. Sri Lanka lose their second review.

OUT! LBW! Another one down and Avishka Fernando goes, taking the review with him. This is brilliant bowling from Sam Curran and he is elated. Full on middle, it swings in. Fernando shuffles and looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. Sam Curran appeals and up goes the finger. Fernando reviews it. The Ball Tracker shows all reds and Sri Lanka lose both their reviews.
Full on off, Fernando drives it through the cover region for a couple of runs.
Avishka Fernando walks out to bat at No.3.
Kusal Perera challenges the umpire for an LBW. No bat involved confirms Ulta Edge. The Ball Tracker shows all three reds. Sri Lanka lose their review.

OUT! LBW! All reds it is and Kusal Perera goes for a duck, taking the review with him. Sam Curran strikes in his first over and Sri Lanka are off to a poor start yet again. Good length ball on middle, Perera looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. An appeal is made for LBW and the finger has gone up. Perera consults his partner and takes the review but in vain as the Ball Tracker shows all reds.
Good length ball on middle, Perera defends it back to the bowler.
Sam Curran to bowl from the other end.
Full on middle, Pathum pushes it to mid on.
Full on middle, Nissanka looks to defend but it goes off the inside edge to square leg.

NOT OUT! There is a big inside edge on this one and Nissanka survives. He knew it. Good length ball on off, Nissanka looks to defend but seems to have taken an inside edge onto the pads. England appeal and after thinking for a while, the umpire gives it out. Nissanka reviews it immediately. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there is a big inside edge on it.
Sri Lanka has taken a review for LBW. There is clearly bat involved confirms Ultra Edge. The on-field decision will be reversed.
FOUR! Lovely way to get off the mark! Full and outside off, Nissanka prods and drives it through the cover region for a boundary.
Good length ball outside off, Nissanka punches it but straight to point.
Willey starts with a full one on off, Nissanka prods and defends it to point.

We are done with the pre-match formalities and we are all set to begin the second ODI! The England players make their way out to the middle, followed by Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera. David Willey will start with the ball.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Perera (WK/C), Avishka Fernando (IN PLACE OF RAMESH MENDIS), Dhananjaya de Silva (IN PLACE OF DHANANJAYA LAKSHAN), Wanindu Hasaranga, Dasun Shanaka, Charith Asalanka, Chamika Karunaratne, Binura Fernando, Dushmantha Chameera, Asitha Fernando (IN PLACE OF PRAVEEN JAYAWICKRAMA).

England (Playing XI) - Jonny Bairstow (WK), Jason Roy (IN PLACE OF LIAM LIVINGSTONE), Joe Root, Eoin Morgan (C), Sam Billings, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, David Willey, Tom Curran (IN PLACE OF CHRIS WOAKES), Adil Rashid, Mark Wood.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of England. They have elected to field first.

Hello all! We are all set for the second ODI between England and Sri Lanka. It has been all England in the limited over series so far and Sri Lanka have surrendered rather meekly. Their bowling has done a good job but their batting shows a sorry picture which they need to rectify before it is too late. The hosts, on the other hand, have been ruthless with the ball and there are slight concerns with the bat. They would look to wrap up the ODI series here itself. Will Sri Lanka be able to level the series or will England continue to dominate? Toss and team updates in a while.
